All members of the team must participate in the presentation, as well as answer any questions. You will be evaluated on how well you demonstrate the 21st Century Skills and meet the performance indicators of this event. Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You and your partner are to assume the roles of marketing director and operations director at NORTHVANE SYSTEMS, a two-year-old manufacturer of smart home sensors and thermostats. The company's chief executive officer (judge), who founded NORTHVANE after fifteen years in commercial building controls, has asked the two of you to review a decision the company must settle before the end of the week.

NORTHVANE sells on one clear advantage: its devices run entirely on a homeowner's own network, with no monthly subscription and no household data leaving the building. Every advertisement and trade show demonstration the company has paid for turns on that promise. Its first round of funding is nearly spent, and a second round depends almost entirely on delivering a pilot installation to CEDARFALL HOTELS, a resort group with properties in four countries.

Assembly is handled by VELDMARK ASSEMBLY, a family-owned plant overseas that accepted NORTHVANE's small orders when larger contractors would not, and that has absorbed three design revisions without repricing. The relationship is informal, conducted in a second language on both sides, and carried largely by the founder's regular visits and long phone calls. VELDMARK's assembly contract comes up for renewal in ninety days.

Last month four thousand units staged for the CEDARFALL pilot were found corroded. The units sat in VELDMARK's warehouse during a humid week in which the facility's climate records show a two-day gap, then travelled in a contracted carrier's trailer through the same weather. Neither record establishes where the moisture reached them, and no further evidence exists.

NORTHVANE's cargo policy would replace the shipment within weeks, but the claim requires one stated cause of loss. Warehouse storage is the cause the insurer has said it would accept, and filing it would send the insurer to VELDMARK for recovery. A narrower claim naming only what the records support would return a fraction of the loss after months of review. Rebuilding the units unclaimed would consume most of the remaining funding, delay the pilot, and postpone the two marketing hires budgeted for the launch.

The chief executive officer (judge) wants your analysis of what the company owes its insurer, its assembler and its investors, and your recommendation on which of the three courses NORTHVANE should take. You will present your recommendation to the chief executive officer (judge) in a meeting. The chief executive officer (judge) will begin the meeting by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the questions, the chief executive officer (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of chief executive officer of NORTHVANE SYSTEMS, a two-year-old manufacturer of smart home sensors and thermostats. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the marketing director and the operations director to analyze what the company owes its insurer, its assembler and its investors, and to recommend whether NORTHVANE should file the cargo claim naming warehouse storage as the cause of loss, file a narrower claim for only the portion the records support, or absorb the loss and rebuild the shipment.

During the presentation you will ask each participant team the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would this decision change the way we work with our assembler?
If we have to file another claim next year, what will this one have taught our insurer about us?
